items.title: Jerome Richardson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 9, 1996
items.q: I can talk about how great Clark Terry is for years and years, you know, and how wonderful he is.

ctx.x: No kidding. Well I hope it works out for you. Sometimes the business of music can — sometimes it’s good to handle it by yourself and then sometimes —

Well I find that it’s very hard to advertise yourself, to talk about yourself. I will never forget one day, it was in Hollywood, I wanted to play in one of these new places. So I made an appointment with the owner of the place. And I walked in and it was a lady. So she looked at me and I looked at her. And we looked at each other for a minute. She said, “Well tell me about yourself.” I said, oh — you know — and I said well I have a bio here. She said no. She really stuck me in the middle. And so I did what I…

items.title: Terry Clark — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Jerome Richardson. They all came in a band collectively from California.

ctx.x: Marshal Royal, Ernie Royal. I don’t know whether – is Jerome Richardson from there?

Jerome Richardson. They all came in a band collectively from California. They were recruited like we were in St. Louis, but we were already ensconced there. We had the upper hand. They came in as a bunch of recruits. I think it might have been pre­ arranged, but they were to have been trained at Great Lakes and formed into a band and sent back to some base in – I think it was Treasure Island in California.
Gerald Wilson was part of that?
